Botanical line drawing: the narrow, thread-like leaf segments and small flower umbrellas, with the fruit enlarged.
Botanical line drawing: finely divided parsley-like leaves and the small flower umbrellas, with the flower and fruit enlarged.
Flower umbrellas going to seed: many small heads on radiating stalks.
The leaf: broad, lobed and toothed like a maple leaf, much larger than any hemlock leaflet.
Botanical line drawing: the large lobed leaf, the flat flower head and the flattened fruit.
Botanical line drawing: the cluster of six-petalled star flowers, the narrow leaves and the bulb.
Botanical line drawing: the trumpet flower, the strap-shaped leaves and the bulb.
Botanical line drawing: two broad leaves with parallel veins and the arching stalk of small nodding bell flowers.
Black-and-white photograph of a flowering stem: hood-shaped flowers and deeply cut hand-shaped leaves.
Botanical line drawing: the stem with hooded flowers and a deeply lobed leaf.
Botanical line drawing: the deeply divided finger-like leaves and the spurred flowers along the stalk.
A cluster of glossy red berries on green stalks above the large toothed, divided leaves.
Botanical line drawing: the divided toothed leaf, the round flower head and the berry cluster.
The plant in flower in shady woods: divided leaves and a single upright white flower head.
The fluffy white flower head held above the toothed leaflets.
Botanical line drawing: the divided leaf, the flower head and the berries on thick stalks.
Flowering stems: small pale yellow buttercup flowers and the elongated green seed heads.
The glossy, rounded, deeply lobed basal leaves.
Botanical line drawing: the branching plant with lobed leaves, small flowers and cylindrical seed heads.
Botanical line drawing: the toothed leaf, the long trumpet flower, and the egg-shaped seed pod covered in spines.
Yellow marble-sized berries hanging from a dry stem in late season.
Botanical line drawing: prickly lobed leaves, star-shaped flowers with a central cone, and the round berries.
Botanical line drawing: narrow wavy-edged leaves on a prickly stem, star-shaped flowers and round berries.
Botanical line drawing: the lobed leaves, the veined funnel flowers and the capped seed pods.
A flower spike (raceme): small whitish flowers on short stalks along a central stem, before the berries form.
Botanical line drawing: the large smooth leaves, the long flower and berry clusters, and a flattened ribbed berry.
THE DEADLY PART: the shiny, mottled, bean-like seeds (each about half an inch long). A child who chews a few can die.
Botanical line drawing: the large star-shaped leaf with pointed lobes and the spiny seed capsule.
The whole plant on open prairie ground: upper leaves edged in white, giving a snowy look from a distance.
Botanical line drawing: the oval leaves, the white-margined upper leaves around the small flowers, and the seed capsule.
A flat mat creeping over concrete: reddish wiry stems with small paired oval leaves.
Close view of the small paired leaves and tiny flowers along the stems. Break a stem: the sap is milky.
Botanical line drawing: the sprawling branched stem with small paired leaves, with leaf and seed enlarged.
A young plant: narrow paired leaves on an upright stem, the stage confused with milkweed shoots.
Botanical line drawing: paired oval leaves, the clusters of small bell flowers, and the long thin seed pods.
Black-and-white photograph of twigs: flat needles in two rows and the cup-shaped berry-like cones with the seed visible.
Botanical line drawing: a branch with flat needles in two rows, with the berry-like cone enlarged.
A husked buckeye fruit hanging among the hand-shaped leaves.
The leaves: five narrow toothed leaflets spreading from one point, like an open hand. Chestnut leaves are single.
Botanical line drawing: the hand-shaped leaf, the flower cluster, and the prickly husk.
Black-and-white photograph: a hand-shaped leaf of five leaflets with smooth round husks.
The nuts: glossy, dark, rounded, each with a large pale "eye". These are poisonous, not chestnuts.
Botanical line drawing: the hand-shaped leaf, the flower cluster and a split husk with the nut.
A single glossy buckeye nut with its pale scar. Poisonous.
Black-and-white photograph of a pressed branch: hand-shaped leaves and the long tube-shaped flowers.
Botanical line drawing: the hand-shaped leaf, the tube flowers and the smooth husk.
Black-and-white photograph: the husks with short stout spikes, split to show the large glossy nuts. Compare the long dense needles of a true chestnut bur.
Botanical line drawing: the hand-shaped leaf of seven leaflets, the flower cluster, the spiky husk and the nut.
Botanical line drawing: the deeply cut ragged leaves and the flat-topped cluster of daisy-like flower heads.
Botanical line drawing: the lobed leaves, the small rayless flower heads with dark-tipped bracts, and a seed with its fluff.
Botanical line drawing: the fern-like, deeply cut leaves and the flat cluster of button flower heads.
The green burs, densely covered in hooked spines, on the plant.
Mature burs about an inch long, covered in hooked spines (scale bar 1 cm).
Botanical line drawing: the rough triangular lobed leaves and a bur.
